chapter: The Original Dixieland band to California
title: How the Hot Five differed from other bands
summary: Joe says no band sounded like the Hot Five because no one else had a Louis Armstrong, though Guy Kelly had a similar combo.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Did you ever hear any of the bands in New Orleans, Baton Rouge or anywhere play any of the kind of same music as the Hot Fives, or was it different...? When you hear the records of Louis with the Hot Five, was that how any of the bands played, or was it completely...
Yeah, it was different. Nobody played like that for the simple reason that nobody had a Louis Armstrong. That was one reason.

Let me hit it another way. The records you listened of the Hot Five, like you were saying, 'Heebie-Jeebies' and 'Cornet Chop Suey,' if you took Louis out of the band, the rest of the group, like Johnny Dodds and Ory, were they playing like the bands you'd heard, the rest of the bands, or did the whole of the Hot Five play different than the band in New Orleans, would you say?
They had something different about them. And one thing was Louis inspired them and everything. There was never a combo that sounded like them...
I think when I went back to Baton Rouge, for that brief time I was there, Guy Kelly had a little combo, something similar to that.
